headline: At least 5 Bangladeshis killed in Kolkata hotel fire
summary: A cosmetics trader from Savar and a journalist from Kushtia with his family were among the victims of the blaze that killed nine people in total.
details: At least five Bangladeshi nationals have been identified among the nine people killed in a hotel fire in central Kolkata early today, according to the Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Among the victims is 37-year-old Ahmed Babu, a cosmetics trader from Savar, who was on a routine business trip to India. He is survived by his wife and two children, aged 12 and 6.
Another victim was a journalist from Kushtia, who died along with three of his family members, including his wife, child, and father-in-law.
Ahmed Babu's family in Savar is in mourning, with relatives and neighbors gathering to support the wife and children left behind.
The Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs is coordinating with Indian authorities to repatriate the bodies of the deceased Bangladeshis.
The State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Shama Obaed, and the Ministry have also launched an emergency helpline for Bangladeshis in Kolkata to provide assistance.
caption:
A devastating hotel fire in Kolkata has claimed the lives of at least five Bangladeshis, including a father of two and a journalist.

At least five Bangladeshi nationals have been identified among the nine people killed in a hotel fire in central Kolkata early today, according to the Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Among the victims is 37-year-old Ahmed Babu, a cosmetics trader from Savar, who was on a routine business trip to India. He is survived by his wife and two children, aged 12 and 6.

Another victim was a journalist from Kushtia, who died along with three of his family members, including his wife, child, and father-in-law.

Ahmed Babu's family in Savar is in mourning, with relatives and neighbors gathering to support the wife and children left behind.

The Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs is coordinating with Indian authorities to repatriate the bodies of the deceased Bangladeshis.

The State Minister for Foreign Affairs, Shama Obaed, and the Ministry have also launched an emergency helpline for Bangladeshis in Kolkata to provide assistance.

Source: The Daily Star, Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune, Somoy News

headline_marked: Former Education Minister [[Dipu Moni granted 12-hour parole]] to attend husband's funeral
headline: Former Education Minister Dipu Moni granted 12-hour parole to attend husband's funeral
summary: The former minister is allowed a brief window of release from custody to bid farewell to her husband, Tawfique Nawaz, who has passed away.
details: Former Education Minister Dipu Moni has been granted 12-hour parole from custody to attend the funeral of her husband, Tawfique Nawaz.
The brief release allows her to see the body of her deceased husband and participate in the burial rites.
Dipu Moni's daughter has also been visiting her in prison to request the release on parole for her mother's bereavement.
The authorities have granted this humanitarian request to allow the family to perform the final rites for the deceased.
caption:
A 12-hour window of release. Former Education Minister Dipu Moni is granted parole to bid farewell to her husband.

Former Education Minister Dipu Moni has been granted 12-hour parole from custody to attend the funeral of her husband, Tawfique Nawaz.

The brief release allows her to see the body of her deceased husband and participate in the burial rites.

Dipu Moni's daughter has also been visiting her in prison to request the release on parole for her mother's bereavement.

The authorities have granted this humanitarian request to allow the family to perform the final rites for the deceased.
